hero.intro: Satin, sequins and one very good column gown, chosen for a shorter frame first. We read the length before we fall for the photograph, so the hem lands where you meant it to and the waist seam sits at yours. Look twice: the detail is usually why we bought it.

category.name: Evening
category.description: Gowns, satin and sequins for evenings out, in lengths and shapes that work on a shorter frame. Columns, A-lines and a back slit or two, picked for where the hem lands rather than how the photo looks.

sections.heading: What makes petite dresses evening wear different
paragraphs: An evening dress uses more fabric than anything else in your closet, so a proportion error shows up twice. A hem drawn to brush the floor puddles at your feet instead. A waist seam meant for your narrowest point drifts down toward your hip. Straps cut for a longer torso slide all night. A smaller size rarely fixes any of it, because the pattern was still drawn for a taller frame: the numbers on the tag move, the distances between the seams barely do.

So this edit starts with length, then shape, then shimmer. The metallic column gown on this page lists 63 inches. The pleated satin maxi lists 58 and a half. Those few inches decide whether you are wearing the dress or carrying it, and both numbers sit in the product details where you can hold them against your own shoulder-to-floor measurement before anything goes in a cart.

sections.heading: How we choose: shape before sparkle
paragraphs: We source from Korea and Thailand first, then Vietnam and elsewhere, and we buy by shape. Height comes from an unbroken vertical line, a waist that sits high, and a neckline that opens up the collarbone. Sequins are the easy part, since every boutique page has them. What earns a place on this rail is the piece that makes you stop and look twice at a pleat, a cutaway or a back you were not expecting.
bullets: Column. A bateau neck, a back-baring drape, one long line from shoulder to floor. Nothing interrupts you on the way down.
A-line. Sequins set into a textured knit, a scoop neck, a skirt that skims past the hip. The kindest shape to shorten.
Strapless sweetheart. Gathers and plissé pleating in a silk blend, with a twist detail at the neck. The top does the talking, so the length can stay quiet.
Long-sleeve jersey. A high V-neck, ruching, and an oversized rosette at a cutout waist that marks your waist exactly where it sits.
Maxi with a slit. Zigzag lamé, cutaway shoulders and a high back slit that gives back the leg a long hem borrows.

sections.heading: How to wear it: three evenings, three dresses
paragraphs: Start with the evening, then the shape, then let the shoes set the hem. Each of these uses one dress from this edit and two things already in your closet, because a look that needs five new pieces is not a look, it is a shopping list.
bullets: Prom. The petite dresses prom night asks for are the ones you can dance in for four hours. A sequin A-line that skims instead of clinging, a strappy sandal you can stand up in, hair up so the neckline gets its moment, and a read of your school dress code before you click buy.

A party that starts late. Search petite dresses party and you get bodycon, over and over. We would rather send you out in the chain mail miniskirt with a plain fitted top, or the long-sleeve jersey gown with nothing on it but earrings.

Dinner, gala, the anniversary one. The pieces we file under petite dresses special occasion are the ones that go to more than one event. Pleated satin maxi, a pointed-toe pump, a small clutch, and a wrap you can drop the minute the room warms up.

sections.heading: Fit and sizing, measured not guessed
paragraphs: Sizing from Korea and Thailand runs on its own scale, so we give you measurements instead of promises. Take three of your own and keep them in your phone: bust, natural waist, and shoulder down to the point where you want the hem to land, in the heels you plan to wear all night. Then hold those against the numbers on the listing. Our size guide shows where to put the tape and what to do when you land between two sizes.

One honest note about length. A plain or A-line hem shortens cleanly and cheaply at a local alterations shop. A pleated, sequined or beaded hem is a longer job, so it is worth deciding that before you buy rather than after. If a piece still arrives wrong, the steps are on the returns page, and you can message us on a weekday through contacts. If the evening in hand is someone else's wedding, the wedding guest edit sits right next door.

sections.heading: New pieces, small batches
paragraphs: We buy in small runs, partly on purpose and partly because that is how this kind of sourcing works. A gown lands in a handful of sizes, sells through, and the next order is rarely the same gown. That is the trade for clothes you will not meet on every boutique page, and for evening shopping it has one plain consequence: if there is a date in your calendar and the dress is right, waiting for a sale usually means watching it go.

It also means the rail keeps moving through the year instead of arriving in two big seasonal drops, so it pays to look again in a few weeks. Or let us do the looking. Leave your email and the next finds reach you while the middle sizes are still on the page. Oops, mine.

sections.heading: What people ask before they buy
paragraphs: Type petite dress evening into a search bar and you get the same three silhouettes, in the same two lengths, on a model who is not petite at all. Here is what people are really asking underneath that search, with the short answers we would give you over a message.
bullets: Is petite a size or a length? A length, mostly. It describes a frame around 5 feet 4 and under, with a shorter torso and a shorter leg, not a narrower body.
Can I wear a maxi at 5 feet 2? Yes. Pick a high waist, a column cut or a slit, then compare the listed length with your shoulder-to-floor measurement in heels.
Does everything need hemming? No. Check the length in the product details first. Plenty of these sit where they should, and the rest are usually a small job.
What about long sleeves? They work when the cuff stops at your wrist bone. Past that a gown reads borrowed, so push the sleeve up or go sleeveless.

Heels or flats? Heel height is part of the hem. The pumps and sandals in this edit list heels from three and a half to four and three-quarter inches, so choose the shoe first and judge the dress second.

faqs.q: What dress length works best if I am 5 feet 2?
faqs.a: Measure from your shoulder to the point where you want the hem to land, wearing the shoes you will keep on, then compare that with the length printed in the product details. Column and A-line shapes usually need the least adjustment, because the line runs straight down. A high waist seam buys you extra leg with no alteration at all.

faqs.q: Are these dresses suitable for prom?
faqs.a: Many of them are. Look for a shape you can sit and dance in for a long evening, a neckline and hemline that meet your school dress code, and straps or sleeves that stay put without being adjusted. A sequin A-line is the easy answer, and a floor-length column works well as long as the hem clears your shoes.

faqs.q: Can one evening dress go to more than one event?
faqs.a: That is how we buy. A pleated satin maxi with a pump and a clutch reads formal. The same dress with a flat sandal and a wrap reads like dinner with friends. Changing shoes, earrings and a jacket does more than changing dresses, and it means the piece earns its place instead of hanging there for one night.

faqs.q: How do I know the size will fit when the piece is sourced from Asia?
faqs.a: Go by measurements rather than the letter on the tag. Sizing from Korea and Thailand runs on its own scale, so each piece lists its own numbers and our size guide shows where to put the tape. If you land between two sizes, size up for a gown with a fitted waist and stay where you are for anything cut loose.

Rarely the same one. We buy small batches from sellers who move on quickly, so a restock is the exception rather than the plan. If a dress is on your list for an evening that already has a date, treat it as now or never, and join the email list so the next arrivals reach you before the rail thins out.
